The title is how you find a test in the output when it fails. This rule reports a title that is empty, starts or ends with a space, or repeats the name of its function, as in `test("test adds an item")`. It also reports a test title that is not a string. Options let you add naming rules of your own.

`--fix` removes the spaces and the repeated word. It changes nothing in a file that uses `toMatchSnapshot()` or `toThrowErrorMatchingSnapshot()`, because snapshots are stored under the title of their test.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 5} */}
```ts
import { describe, test } from "bun:test";

describe("describe cart", () => {
  test("", () => {});
  test(" adds an item", () => {});
  test("test removes an item", () => {});
  test(404, () => {});
});
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```ts
import { describe, test } from "bun:test";

describe("cart", () => {
  test("adds an item", () => {});
  test(`removes ${count} items`, () => {});
  test("responds to " + path, () => {});
});
```

`bun test` takes a function, a class or a number as the title of a `describe`, so that is allowed by default:

{/* good */}
```ts
import { describe, test } from "bun:test";

describe(Cart, () => {
  test("adds an item", () => {});
});
```

## Options

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `allowArguments` | `false` | Allow a title that is a plain variable, such as `title`. |
| `ignoreTypeOfDescribeName` | `true` | Allow a `describe` title that is not a string. |
| `ignoreTypeOfTestName` | `false` | Allow a `test` or `it` title that is not a string. |
| `ignoreSpaces` | `false` | Allow spaces at the start and the end. |
| `disallowedWords` | `[]` | Whole words that a title cannot contain. Case does not matter. |
| `mustMatch` | none | A pattern that every title has to match. |
| `mustNotMatch` | none | A pattern that no title can match. |

A variable as the title of a test is reported by default, because the rule cannot tell what it holds:

{/* bad */}
```ts
import { test } from "bun:test";

test(title, () => {});
```

{/* good {"options": [{"allowArguments": true}]} */}
```ts
import { test } from "bun:test";

test(title, () => {});
```

{/* bad {"options": [{"ignoreTypeOfDescribeName": false}]} */}
```ts
import { describe, test } from "bun:test";

describe(Cart, () => {
  test("adds an item", () => {});
});
```

{/* bad {"options": [{"disallowedWords": ["should"]}]} */}
```ts
import { test } from "bun:test";

test("Should add an item", () => {});
```

`mustMatch` and `mustNotMatch` take a regular expression as a string, either `"^adds "` or `"/^adds /i"`. Of the flags only `i` has an effect. To set the message of the report, pass `[pattern, message]`:

{/* bad {"options": [{"mustNotMatch": ["\\.$", "Do not end a title with a period"]}]} */}
```ts
import { test } from "bun:test";

test("adds an item.", () => {});
```

To use a different pattern for `describe`, `test` and `it`, pass an object. Each value is a pattern. A function that is not in the object is not checked:

{/* bad {"options": [{"mustMatch": {"it": "^should "}}], "count": 1} */}
```ts
import { it, test } from "bun:test";

it("adds an item", () => {});

test("adds an item", () => {});
```
